claim: Glaucoma will affect more than 100 million individuals between 40 and 80 years of age by 2040.
source: Glaucoma is the most common cause of irreversible blindness and will affect more than 100 million individuals between 40 and 80 years of age by 2040 (Tham et al., 2014).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Tham et al., 2014.

claim: Annual direct medical costs to treat glaucoma in 2 million patients in the United States totaled $2.9 billion.
source: Annual direct medical costs to treat this disease in 2 million patients in the United States totaled $2.9 billion (Varma et al., 2011).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Varma et al., 2011.

claim: Glaucoma is characterized by injury to the axons of retinal ganglion cells followed by progressive degeneration of RGC somata and axons within the retina and Wallerian degeneration of the myelinated axons in the optic nerve.
source: Glaucoma is a neurodegenerative disease characterized by injury to the axons of retinal ganglion cells (RGCs) followed by progressive degeneration of RGC somata and axons within the retina and Wallerian degeneration of the myelinated axons in the optic nerve (ON) (Quigley, 1993; Quigley et al., 1995; Libby et al., 2005; Howell et al., 2007; Weinreb and Khaw, 2004; Calkins, 2012; Burgoyne, 2011; Nickells et al., 2012; Jonas et al., 2017).
evidence: The claim is supported by multiple citations to published literature.

claim: The level of intraocular pressure is the most common risk factor for glaucoma.
source: The level of intraocular pressure (IOP) is the most common risk factor (Singh and Shrivastava, 2009).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Singh and Shrivastava, 2009.

claim: Current clinical therapies target reduction of IOP to retard glaucomatous neurodegeneration.
source: Current clinical therapies target reduction of IOP to retard glaucomatous neurodegeneration (The AGIS Investigators, 2000; Early Manifest Glaucoma Trial Group et al., 2002; Lichter et al., 2001), but neuroprotectants are critically needed to prevent degeneration of RGCs and ON.
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to clinical trial publications.

claim: Intracameral injection of SO forms a droplet in the anterior chamber that contacts the surface of the iris and tightly seals the pupil due to high surface tension.
source: As illustrated in Figure 1A,B and Video 1, after intracameral injection SO forms a droplet in the anterior chamber that contacts the surface of the iris and tightly seals the pupil due to high surface tension.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental observations shown in Figure 1A,B and Video 1.

claim: In SO-injected eyes, no injected dye reached the anterior chamber, indicating that SO causes effective pupillary block.
source: In dramatic contrast to a normal naïve eye, in which copious dye passed through the pupil and appeared in the anterior chamber almost immediately after injection, no injected dye reached the anterior chamber of the SO eye (Videos 2 and 3). This result indicates that SO causes effective pupillary block.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Videos 2 and 3.

claim: IOP was lower in the SO eyes than in CL eyes when measured immediately after anesthetizing the animals with isoflurane.
source: Surprisingly, IOP was lower in the SO eyes than in CL eyes when measured immediately after anesthetizing the animals with isoflurane (Figure 1C).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1C.

claim: IOP of the SO eyes was progressively and significantly elevated over extended periods of time, in dramatic contrast to the CL eyes, in which IOP decreased over time.
source: Measurements over extended periods of time showed the IOP of the SO eyes to be progressively and significantly elevated, in dramatic contrast to the CL eyes, in which IOP decreased over time.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental measurements described in the text and shown in Figure 1C.

claim: Pupillary size reached its maximum and IOP reached to its plateau about 12–15 min after induction of anesthesia with continuous isoflurane inhalation.
source: Pupillary size reached its maximum and IOP reached to its plateau about 12–15 min after induction of anesthesia with continuous isoflurane inhalation.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental observations described in the text.

claim: IOP elevation in the SO eye started as early as 2 days post injection and remained stable for at least 8 weeks at an IOP about 2.5 fold that of CL eyes, if the diameter of the SO droplet was larger than 1.5 mm.
source: IOP elevation in the SO eye started as early as 2 days post injection (2dpi) and remained stable for at least 8 weeks (the longest time point we tested) at an IOP about 2.5 fold that of CL eyes, if the diameter of the SO droplet was larger than 1.5 mm (Figure 1D).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1D.

claim: In mice with a small SO droplet (≤1.5 mm), the IOP initially increased but dropped soon afterwards.
source: We achieved this size of SO droplet in about 80% of mice, but in the 20% of mice with a small SO droplet (≤1.5 mm) in the anterior chamber due to poor injection or oil leaking, in which the IOP initially increased but dropped soon afterwards (Figure 1D).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1D.

claim: GCC in SOHU eyes became gradually and progressively thinner at 1, 3, 5, and 8 weeks post injection.
source: GCC in SOHU eyes became gradually and progressively thinner (about 84%, 65%, 61% and 53% of CL eyes) at 1, 3, 5, and 8 weeks post injection (wpi).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental measurements described in the text and shown in Figure 2A,B.

claim: GCC thinning is statistically significant at 5 and 8 wpi compared to 1 wpi.
source: GCC thinning is statistically significant at 5 and 8 wpi compared to 1 wpi (Figure 2A,B).
evidence: The claim is supported by statistical analysis of experimental data shown in Figure 2A,B.

claim: The visual acuity of SOHU eyes decreased rapidly at 1wpi.
source: The visual acuity of SOHU eyes decreased rapidly at 1wpi, which may due to the presence of SO in the anterior chamber.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental measurements described in the text and shown in Figure 2C.

claim: The further decreased visual acuity at 5 and 8 wpi compared to 1 wpi indicates progressive visual function deficits in the SOHU eyes.
source: However, the further decreased visual acuity at 5 and 8 wpi compared to 1 wpi indicates progressive visual function deficits in the SOHU eyes (Figure 2C).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2C.

claim: The P1-N2 amplitude ratio of the SO eyes to CL eyes decreased significantly.
source: Consistent with visual acuity deficit, the P1-N2 amplitude ratio of the SO eyes to CL eyes decreased significantly (Figure 2D,E).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2D,E.

claim: There was no statistical significance in surviving RGC counts in the peripheral retina between SOHU and control eyes at 1wpi.
source: Similar to the changes of GCC thickness measured by OCT in vivo, there was no statistical significance in surviving RGC counts in the peripheral retina between SOHU and control eyes at 1wpi, whereas there was significant and worsening RGC loss at 3, 5 and 8wpi, when only 43, 28, and 12% of peripheral RGCs survived (Figure 3A,B).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3A,B.

claim: There was significant and worsening RGC loss at 3, 5 and 8wpi, when only 43, 28, and 12% of peripheral RGCs survived.
source: Similar to the changes of GCC thickness measured by OCT in vivo, there was no statistical significance in surviving RGC counts in the peripheral retina between SOHU and control eyes at 1wpi, whereas there was significant and worsening RGC loss at 3, 5 and 8wpi, when only 43, 28, and 12% of peripheral RGCs survived (Figure 3A,B).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3A,B.

claim: Significant RGC axon degeneration occurred in SOHU ONs; only 57, 41% and 35% RGC axons survived at 3, 5, and 8wpi.
source: Significant RGC axon degeneration also occurred in SOHU ONs; only 57, 41% and 35% RGC axons survived at 3, 5, and 8wpi (Figure 3A,C).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3A,C.

claim: SO intravitreal injection did not cause significant IOP elevation, visual function deficits, or RGC/ON degeneration at 8wpi.
source: First, SO intravitreal injection did not cause significant IOP elevation, visual function deficits, or RGC/ON degeneration at 8wpi (Figure 4A–F).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4A–F.

claim: Eyes with small SO droplets (≤1.5 mm) and unstable IOP elevation showed no significant RGC death or axon degeneration at 8wpi.
source: Second, the eyes with small SO droplets (≤1.5 mm) and unstable IOP elevation (Figure 1D) showed no significant RGC death or axon degeneration at 8wpi (Figure 4G,H).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4G,H.

claim: The neurodegeneration phenotypes observed in SOHU eyes are glaucomatous responses to ocular hypertension.
source: Therefore, we conclude that the neurodegeneration phenotypes observed in SOHU eyes are glaucomatous responses to ocular hypertension.
evidence: The claim is based on inference from the experimental results showing that SO toxicity alone does not cause neurodegeneration.

claim: Flushing out the SO from the anterior chamber lowered the IOP back to normal quickly and stably.
source: However, we were able to flush out the SO from the anterior chamber with the aid of normal saline infiltration (Figure 5A, Video 5). This procedure lowered the IOP back to normal quickly and stably (Figure 5B), suggesting that SOHU is a reversible model that can be used to test whether lowering IOP affects degeneration of glaucomatous RGCs or the combination effect with neuroprotection.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5A,B and Video 5.

claim: SOHU is a reversible model that can be used to test whether lowering IOP affects degeneration of glaucomatous RGCs or the combination effect with neuroprotection.
source: This procedure lowered the IOP back to normal quickly and stably (Figure 5B), suggesting that SOHU is a reversible model that can be used to test whether lowering IOP affects degeneration of glaucomatous RGCs or the combination effect with neuroprotection.
evidence: The claim is based on inference from the experimental observation that SO removal reverses IOP elevation.

claim: Secondary glaucoma with acutely elevated IOP occurs as a post-operative complication following the intravitreal use of silicone oil in human vitreoretinal surgery.
source: Secondary glaucoma with acutely elevated IOP occurs as a post-operative complication following the intravitreal use of silicone oil (SO) in human vitreoretinal surgery (Ichhpujani et al., 2009; Kornmann and Gedde, 2016).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to published literature.

claim: SO is used as a tamponade in retinal detachment repair because of its buoyancy and high surface tension.
source: SO is used as a tamponade in retinal detachment repair because of its buoyancy and high surface tension.
evidence: The claim is based on established clinical knowledge.

claim: SO is lighter than the aqueous and vitreous fluids and an excess can physically occlude the pupil, which prevents aqueous flow into the anterior chamber.
source: However, SO is lighter than the aqueous and vitreous fluids and an excess can physically occlude the pupil, which prevents aqueous flow into the anterior chamber.
evidence: The claim is based on established clinical knowledge.

claim: Pupillary block increases aqueous pressure in the posterior chamber and displaces the iris anteriorly, which causes angle-closure, blockage of aqueous outflow through TM, and a further increase in IOP.
source: This obstruction increases aqueous pressure in the posterior chamber and displace the iris anteriorly, which causes angle-closure, blockage of aqueous outflow through TM, and a further increase in IOP.
evidence: The claim is based on established clinical knowledge.

claim: Prophylactic peripheral iridotomy that maintains the circulation between anterior and posterior chambers normally prevents this type of secondary glaucoma.
source: Prophylactic peripheral iridotomy that maintains the circulation between anterior and posterior chambers normally prevents this type of secondary glaucoma.
evidence: The claim is based on established clinical knowledge.

claim: After intracameral injection, SO forms a droplet in the anterior chamber that contacts the surface of the iris and tightly seals the pupil due to high surface tension.
source: As illustrated in Figure 1A,B and Video 1, after intracameral injection SO forms a droplet in the anterior chamber that contacts the surface of the iris and tightly seals the pupil due to high surface tension.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental observations shown in Figure 1A,B and Video 1.

claim: The ciliary body constantly produces aqueous humor, which accumulates in the posterior chamber and pushes the iris forward.
source: The ciliary body constantly produces aqueous humor, which accumulates in the posterior chamber and pushes the iris forward.
evidence: The claim is based on established anatomical and physiological knowledge.

claim: When the iris root touches the posterior corneal surface, the anterior chamber angle closes.
source: When the iris root touches the posterior corneal surface, the anterior chamber angle closes (Figure 1A), as evidenced by live anterior chamber optical coherence tomography (OCT) (Figure 1B).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental observations shown in Figure 1A,B.

claim: Dilation of the pupil until it is larger than the SO droplet can relieve the pupillary block.
source: Dilation of the pupil until it is larger than the SO droplet can relieve the pupillary block.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental observations described in the text and shown in Video 4.

claim: After pupil dilation, aqueous humor floods into the anterior chamber and pushes the SO droplet away from the iris, which reopens the anterior chamber angle.
source: Video 4 shows that after pupil dilation aqueous humor floods into the anterior chamber and pushes the SO droplet away from the iris, which reopens the anterior chamber angle (Figure 1A,B).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental observations shown in Video 4 and Figure 1A,B.

claim: The increasing IOP in the SO eyes closely correlated with the change in pupillary size, indicating a significant role of pupillary block.
source: The increasing IOP in the SO eyes closely correlated with the change in pupillary size, indicating a significant role of pupillary block.
evidence: The claim is based on inference from the experimental observation of correlation between IOP and pupillary size.

claim: Pupillary dilation removed the pupillary block and allowed the tonometer to detect higher IOP after aqueous humor migration into the anterior chamber, which reflects the elevated IOP in the posterior segment of the eye.
source: Pupillary dilation removed the pupillary block and allowed the tonometer to detect higher IOP after aqueous humor migration into the anterior chamber, which reflects the elevated IOP in the posterior segment of the eye.
evidence: The claim is based on inference from the experimental observations of IOP changes after pupillary dilation.

claim: In mice in which IOP was measured for as long as 30 min under anesthesia, the IOP eventually declined, indicating effective TM clearance of aqueous during this time.
source: In mice in which we measured IOP for as long as 30 min under anesthesia, however, the IOP eventually declined, indicating effective TM clearance of aqueous during this time (Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: The claim is based on inference from the experimental observation of IOP decline over extended measurement periods.

claim: The thickness of the retinal nerve fiber layer measured by posterior OCT serves as a reliable biomarker for glaucomatous RGC degeneration.
source: Clinically, the thickness of the retinal nerve fiber layer (RNFL) measured by posterior OCT serves as a reliable biomarker for glaucomatous RGC degeneration (Balcer et al., 2015; Aktas et al., 2016; Costello et al., 2006).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to published literature.

claim: OKR is a natural reflex that objectively assesses mouse visual acuity.
source: OKR is a natural reflex that objectively assesses mouse visual acuity (Prusky et al., 2004; Douglas et al., 2005).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to published literature.

claim: The mouse eye will only track a grating stimulus that is moving from the temporal to nasal visual field, which allows both eyes to be measured independently.
source: The mouse eye will only track a grating stimulus that is moving from the temporal to nasal visual field, which allows both eyes to be measured independently (Douglas et al., 2005; Douglas et al., 2006).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to published literature.

claim: OKR has been used to establish correlations between visual deficit and RGC loss in the DBA/2 glaucoma mouse model.
source: It has been used to establish correlations between visual deficit and RGC loss in the DBA/2 glaucoma mouse model (Burroughs et al., 2011).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to published literature.

claim: PERG is an important electrophysiological assessment of general RGC function, in which the ERG responses are stimulated with contrast-reversing horizontal bars alternating at constant mean luminance.
source: PERG is an important electrophysiological assessment of general RGC function, in which the ERG responses are stimulated with contrast-reversing horizontal bars alternating at constant mean luminance (Porciatti, 2015).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to published literature.

claim: IOP elevation in SOHU mouse eyes produces glaucomatous RGC and ON degeneration that starts as early as 3wpi and becomes progressing more severe at later time points that correlate with visual function deficits.
source: Therefore, IOP elevation in SOHU mouse eyes produces glaucomatous RGC and ON degeneration that starts as early as 3wpi and becomes progressing more severe at later time points that correlate with visual function deficits.
evidence: The claim is based on inference from the experimental data showing progressive RGC and axon loss correlating with visual function deficits.

claim: SOHU eyes developed progressive structural and visual function deficits that closely resemble changes in glaucoma patients.
source: Taken together, these in vivo results show that SOHU eyes developed progressive structural and visual function deficits that closely resemble changes in glaucoma patients.
evidence: The claim is based on inference from the experimental results and comparison to clinical knowledge.

claim: RGCs are very sensitive to IOP elevation, but resilient for a period of time before further degeneration.
source: Nevertheless, these results suggest that RGCs are very sensitive to IOP elevation, but resilient for a period of time before further degeneration.
evidence: The claim is based on inference from the experimental observations of early functional deficits followed by progressive structural degeneration.

claim: Direct injection of SO into the anterior chamber of mice would be more efficient than intravitreal injection, preventing the need to remove the vitreous and reducing toxicity due to direct contact with the retina.
source: Although intravitreal injection of SO in vitreoretinal surgeries can cause post-operative secondary glaucoma in humans (Ichhpujani et al., 2009; Kornmann and Gedde, 2016), we reasoned that direct injection of SO into the anterior chamber of mice would be more efficient, preventing the need to remove the vitreous and reducing toxicity due to direct contact with the retina.
evidence: The claim is based on speculation about the advantages of intracameral versus intravitreal injection.

claim: SO itself may blur vision or affect the visual function assays because its optical characteristics differ from those of aqueous humor.
source: One caveat, however, is that SO itself in anterior chamber may blur vision or affect the visual function assays because its optical characteristics differ from those of aqueous humor.
evidence: The claim is based on speculation about potential confounding effects of SO on visual function measurements.

claim: It is possible that deficits in visual function precede morphological changes, or that there is no proportional relationship between RGC function and RGC morphology.
source: It is also possible that deficits in visual function precede morphological changes, or that there is no proportional relationship between RGC function and RGC morphology, since the visual acuity and PERG amplitude are not always correlated with RGC numbers.
evidence: The claim is based on speculation about the relationship between functional and morphological changes.

claim: The SOHU model is excellent for deciphering the key components of the degeneration cascade associated with ocular hypertension, but it is not suitable for TM function/deficit studies because it depends on pupillary block and spares TM.
source: The SOHU model is excellent for deciphering the key components of the degeneration cascade associated with ocular hypertension, but it is not suitable for TM function/deficit studies because it depends on pupillary block and spares TM.
evidence: The claim is based on inference from the mechanism of the SOHU model.

claim: The SOHU model has features of acute secondary glaucoma in humans.
source: Because the IOP elevation is rapid and neurodegeneration severe within a few weeks, the SOHU model has features of acute secondary glaucoma in humans, but the extent to which it also mimics more chronic and milder primary glaucoma in patients needs further investigation.
evidence: The claim is based on inference from the characteristics of the SOHU model.

claim: Human secondary angle-closure glaucoma is accompanied by RGC and significant photoreceptor loss.
source: Human secondary angle-closure glaucoma is accompanied by RGC and significant photoreceptor loss (Panda and Jonas, 1992; Janssen et al., 1996; Nork et al., 2000), which may at least in part be due to ischemia caused by high IOP.
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to published literature.

claim: Decreased blood flow through the choroidal circulation and ophthalmic artery has been reported in primary open angle glaucoma patients.
source: Decreased blood flow through the choroidal circulation and ophthalmic artery has been reported in primary open angle glaucoma patients as well (Rojanapongpun et al., 1993; Michelson et al., 1995; Cellini et al., 1996; Yamazaki and Drance, 1997; Butt et al., 1997; Kaiser et al., 1997; Yin et al., 1997).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to published literature.

claim: A modified SOHU model that induces and maintains a moderate elevation of IOP through frequent pupil dilation may more closely reproduce the features of clinical primary open angle glaucoma.
source: A modified SOHU model that induces and maintains a moderate elevation of IOP through frequent pupil dilation may more closely reproduce the features of clinical primary open angle glaucoma.
evidence: The claim is based on speculation about potential modifications to the SOHU model.

claim: This novel mouse acute ocular hypertension glaucoma model replicates secondary post-operative glaucoma.
source: In summary, this novel mouse acute ocular hypertension glaucoma model replicates secondary post-operative glaucoma.
evidence: The claim is based on inference from the experimental results and comparison to clinical conditions.

claim: The SOHU model is straightforward, does not require special equipment or repeat injections, and may be applicable to a range of animal species with only minor modifications.
source: It is straightforward, does not require special equipment or repeat injections, and may be applicable to a range of animal species with only minor modifications.
evidence: The claim is based on inference from the characteristics of the SOHU model and speculation about its applicability to other species.

claim: The SOHU model is easily reversible by removing SO from the anterior chamber and particularly useful for screening neuroprotective therapies in vivo.
source: It is easily reversible by removing SO from the anterior chamber and particularly useful for screening neuroprotective therapies in vivo.
evidence: The claim is based on inference from the experimental demonstration of reversibility.

claim: The SOHU model generates stable, robust IOP elevation and significant neurodegeneration within weeks.
source: Therefore we report this simple, convenient, effective, reproducible, and reversible mouse model that generates stable, robust IOP elevation and significant neurodegeneration within weeks with the hopes that it will standardize assessment of the pathogenesis of ocular hypertension-induced glaucoma and facilitate selection of neuroprotectants for glaucoma.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data presented throughout the manuscript.

claim: Intracameral injection of microbeads to occlude aqueous humor circulation through TM produces excellent IOP elevation and glaucomatous neurodegeneration.
source: Intracameral injection of microbeads to occlude aqueous humor circulation through TM produces excellent IOP elevation and glaucomatous neurodegeneration (Sappington et al., 2010; Chen et al., 2011; Cone et al., 2010; Samsel et al., 2011).

claim: Retaining microbeads at the angle of the anterior chamber and controlling the degree of aqueous outflow blockade are difficult.
source: However, retaining microbeads at the angle of the anterior chamber and controlling the degree of aqueous outflow blockade are difficult.

claim: The microbead model's lengthy duration (6–12 weeks after microbeads injection) causes death of only less than 30% of RGC, leaving a narrow window for preclinical testing of neuroprotective therapies.
source: Furthermore, its lengthy duration (6–12 weeks after microbeads injection) causes death of only less than 30% of RGC (Cone et al., 2010; Ito et al., 2016; Yang et al., 2016), leaving a narrow window for preclinical testing of neuroprotective therapies.

claim: Injection of hypertonic saline and laser photocoagulation of the episcleral veins and TM are commonly used in rats and larger animals.
source: Injection of hypertonic saline and laser photocoagulation of the episcleral veins and TM are commonly used in rats and larger animals (Morrison et al., 2008).

source: Although similar techniques also produce ocular hypertension in mice (Aihara et al., 2003; Grozdanic et al., 2003; Yun et al., 2014), they are technically challenging, and irreversible ocular tissue damage and intraocular inflammation complicate their interpretation (Pang and Clark, 2007; Chen and Zhang, 2015).

claim: Various rodent ocular hypertension models have been developed including spontaneous mutant or transgenic mice and rats and mice with inducible blockage of aqueous humor outflow from the trabecular meshwork.
source: Various rodent ocular hypertension models have been developed including spontaneous mutant or transgenic mice and rats and mice with inducible blockage of aqueous humor outflow from the trabecular meshwork (TM) (Pang and Clark, 2007; Morrison et al., 2008; McKinnon et al., 2009; Chen and Zhang, 2015).

claim: While genetic mouse models are valuable to understand the roles of a specific gene in IOP elevation and/or glaucomatous neurodegeneration, the pathologic effects may take months to years to manifest.
source: While genetic mouse models are valuable to understand the roles of a specific gene in IOP elevation and/or glaucomatous neurodegeneration, the pathologic effects may take months to years to manifest.

source: The rodent serves as the mammalian experimental species of choice for modeling human diseases and large-scale genetic manipulations.
